stem: Dynamic compliance decreases while static compliance is unchanged. Which problem does this pattern suggest?
rationale: Static compliance reflects elastic properties; dynamic includes airway resistance. A drop in dynamic alone → increased airway resistance.

stem: Which change most directly reduces work of breathing in severe asthma?
rationale: WOB in asthma is driven by high airway resistance; bronchodilators reduce resistance and dynamic hyperinflation.

stem: A patient on volume‑control ventilation develops auto‑PEEP. Which adjustment helps most?
options: Lengthen expiratory time (reduce rate or I:E)
rationale: Auto‑PEEP arises from incomplete exhalation; allowing more expiratory time reduces air trapping.

stem: Which bedside measure best reflects adequate inspiratory muscle strength for extubation?
options: MIP (NIF) more negative than −25 cm H2O
rationale: An MIP/NIF more negative than −25 cm H2O supports inspiratory strength; VC ≥10–15 ml/kg and VT ≥5–7 ml/kg are also used.

stem: During transport on 100% O2 via NRB, SpO2 falls from 98% to 82%, and the patient becomes tachypneic. First action?
options: Apply BVM with PEEP and prepare for escalation
rationale: Acute desaturation on NRB suggests failure to ventilate or shunt; immediate assisted ventilation with PEEP may be required.
